dedupe_keys.name: kentucky calibrated models ky17 and ky18 and the federally owned water main system university of kentucky

description: KY17 and KY18 are two hydraulically calibrated Kentucky distribution models, and FOWM is a small federally owned water main system, all contributed by Lindell Ormsbee to the Water Distribution System Research Database. According to the summary spreadsheet, KY17 is the largest network in the database, with 6,567 pipes, 18,280 nodes, 5 pumps, 1 reservoir and 3 tanks, an average demand of 2.91 million gallons per day, and water-quality information; KY18 has 910 pipes, 3,056 nodes, 3 pumps, 2 reservoirs and 3 tanks; FOWM has 22 pipes, 17 nodes and one reservoir. All three are looped and marked calibrated. The index page lists them (entries 17 to 19) without an entry page, download link or DOI, so this record points to the database page and the UKnowledge collection, where the files should be requested. Coverage is regional (Kentucky) for the two utility models; the summary gives no dates. Cost is free, but the pages state no licence, only a copyright notice. Only the index page, the entry pages, the summary spreadsheet and DataCite metadata were read; no network file was downloaded or run. Simulation uses: calibration and water-quality studies, and testing of sampling or leak-detection methods on a large calibrated model. Related records: the database record and EPANET.
